# Motivation: Why Green Code

- **Limitation of R**: interpreted language; cost of loops and dynamic memory allocation; limits of vectorization (e.g., MCMC)
- **Green computing**: computation = electricity = carbon.
Statistical computing is not an exception (cumulative cost of repeated simulations, MCMC, bootstrap)
- **Definition of sustainability for this course**: obtaining the same statistical result with less time, memory, and energy.
Includes the trade-off against development time
- **Energy estimation method**: the Green Algorithms formula [@lannelongue2021]
$$
\text{Energy}=t\times\left(\text{Core Power} + \text{Memory Power}\right)\times\text{Power Usage Effectiveness}
$$
$$
\text{CO2e}=\text{Energy}\times\text{Carbon Intensity}
$$
  - Units: $\text{kWh}=\text{Watt}\times\text{hour}\div1000$
  $$
    \text{CO2e (g)}=\text{Energy (kWh)}\times\text{Carbon Intensity (g/kWh)}
  $$
  - Relation to parallelization: increasing cores k-fold multiplies the core term by exactly k, while $t$ shrinks by at most a factor of $1/k$ (Amdahl's law).
  If speedup is sublinear, time goes down but total energy can go up.
- **Introducing the running example**: the CCPP data, definition of the two tasks (bootstrap / Bayesian regression), and a preview of the five implementations to be compared in Ch10
- First measurement: run both tasks in naive R and record baseline time, memory, and energy
